title: DENDRAL Documented in Stanford Machine-Induction Research Memo
summary: On April 5, 1965, Edward A. Feigenbaum and R. W. Watson issued An Initial Problem Statement for a Machine Induction Research Project at the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Project. The memo described research then getting under way on machine induction using organic chemistry and explicitly documented a system called Dendral as an existing ALGOL program for the B-5000.
significance: A primary-source documentation milestone showing DENDRAL already existed as a named program by April 5, 1965, while separately documenting the planned machine-induction research around it. This record does not treat the memo date as DENDRAL's invention, first implementation, or system-birth date.

verification.note: The archived April 5, 1965 Stanford Artificial Intelligence Project memo directly states that the research project was getting under way and that a system called Dendral existed as an ALGOL program for the B-5000. Edward Feigenbaum's Stanford-hosted archival commentary independently identifies the April 5 plan as the earliest document he wrote about DENDRAL and says the DENDRAL Project had not yet formally been formed. The candidate therefore records a documentation/planning milestone only; no invention date, first-implementation date, formal project-formation date, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship is inferred.
